title: Local finite presentation and unique first order lifting imply etaleness
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume that $f$ is locally of finite presentation, meaning that its maps on etale scheme charts are locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that for every first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], every $a_0:T_0\to X$ and $b:T\to Y$ satisfying $f a_0=b j$ admit exactly one $a:T\to X$ with $a j=a_0$ and $f a=b$. Then $f$ is etale, meaning that the induced morphisms on etale scheme charts are etale scheme morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Fix any commutative chart diagram $v h=f u$, with $U,V$ schemes over $S$, $u:U\to X$ and $v:V\to Y$ representable etale, and $h:U\to V$ an $S$-morphism. The local finite presentation hypothesis gives that $h$ is locally of finite presentation. The lifting hypothesis is exactly $P(f)$ in [lem-sfb-formally-etale-space-chart-locality]. Its forward implication gives $P(h)$ for this diagram: every compatible affine first order lifting problem over $S$ has a unique solution in $U$.

The property $P(h)$ also tests all affine scheme lifting problems required by the scheme criterion, without a preassigned $S$-structure. Indeed, given $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, $a_0:T_0\to U$ and $b:T\to V$ with $h a_0=bj$, give $T$ the structure morphism $T\xrightarrow{b}V\to S$ and $T_0$ its composite with $j$. Since $h$ is over $S$, the equation makes $a_0$ an $S$-morphism. Apply $P(h)$ to obtain its unique lift $a$. Any scheme lift with $ha=b$ is automatically over $S$, since its composite to $S$ equals $(V\to S)ha=(V\to S)b$. Thus uniqueness among $S$-morphisms is uniqueness among all scheme lifts.

source.place: Tag 04GD (lemma-formally-etale), scheme-chart lifting condition; explicit unpacking of the base convention in definition-formally-smooth-etale-unramified.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-unique-infinitesimal-lifts-etale] to the scheme morphism $c=h:U\to V$. Step 1 supplies local finite presentation and step 2 supplies existence and uniqueness for every affine first order thickening, exactly its hypotheses. Hence $h$ is etale. The chart diagram was arbitrary, so every induced morphism on etale scheme charts is etale. This is precisely the meaning of etaleness of $f$ stipulated in the statement, and proves the conclusion.
